papers.title: Longest run for $q$-binary trials
papers.abstract: We investigate the longest-run distribution for binary trials in which the success probability varies geometrically. Exact formulae are derived for the probability mass function and the cumulative distribution function of the length of the longest success run in a sequence of $q$-binary trials, using enumerative combinatorics. The setting covers independent but not necessarily identically distributed zero--one trials whose success probabilities follow a geometric rule, and the classical independent and identically distributed Bernoulli longest-run distribution is recovered in the limit $q\to 1$. A simulation study confirms accurate maximum likelihood estimation of the base success probability and the geometric parameter $q$, a well-calibrated and powerful boundary-corrected likelihood ratio test of the hypothesis that $q=1$, and close agreement between the analytical cumulative distribution function and its empirical counterpart.

papers.title: A nudge among nudges: when the field pushes back
papers.abstract: Behavioural interventions are designed and tested as if the setting they enter stays put. But other actors push the same people, watch the behaviour and respond when it moves. The paper asks what becomes of a nudge in such a field. In an agent-based model, people act when their inclination and the pushes they feel cross a threshold, nudges compete for limited attention, and other actors steer the behaviour's rate towards their own goals without seeing the nudge. Calibrated to published effect sizes, it reproduces four documented regularities, one of them by calibration. The same nudge meets five fates, set by who else acts: attenuated, transient, null, reversed, or a blind site, where a sound field experiment reports nearly the full effect while its site gains little. Where the field reacts, a pilot's own comparison does not forecast the rollout: it cannot see the response the pilot provokes, and a small pilot does not exhaust the competitor as the rollout does. The fate follows from a few quantities, with nothing fitted after the calibration; the derivation matched the simulation on eight of ten maps of settings. Across 49,152 random settings, each with a competitor, the expected effect was the exception; what shifted the fate most depended on how attention is shared: the nudge's strength when the strongest nudge is heard first, the number of competing nudges when it is split. Whether a real field reacts can be read from marks a trial could record, such as drift among the untreated.
